text:
olivia: Quick report from this morning's onboard of aurora-lite-int4 on the structured-output path. We started to see funcall consumers complain about missing required keys for the `create_ticket` tool around 09:12 UTC. Roughly 0.4% of calls failed schema validation downstream.
raj: Can you drop a couple of raw outputs so we can see the failure mode?
olivia: Yep, grabbed a few from the canary logs. notice the key names and ordering variance:
```
{"tool":"create_ticket","params":{"title":"Login fails","desc":"user sees 500"}}
{"tool":"create_ticket","params":{"desc":"user sees 500","title":"Login fails"}}
{"tool":"create_ticket","params":{"title":"Login fails"}}  
```
lin: Hmm first two are semantically identical (ordering difference) but third is missing `desc`. Our JSON parser accepts both ordering but our call-contract linter requires `desc` present and non-empty. Seems int4 decoding occasionally drops short strings from the tail of the params object.
ciara: Any correlation with sequence length or kv-cache behavior?
olivia: Correlated with responses that hit the 256 token boundary and used the sampled tail trimming config. Also higher incidence when the model runs in `streaming=true` mode.
raj: Do we know if the key is dropped at generation time or during our post-processing trimming? Could be the tokenizer splitting the `desc` string across token boundary and trimming removed it.
lin: I ran a binary diff between full float canary outputs and int4 canary; the float path retains desc in 99.98% of samples, int4 drops desc around 0.38% in the specific traffic slice.
ciara: Proposed mitigations: 
- add `schema_lint: soft` on the routing layer to convert key-order variations to accepted form (i.e., treat object fields as unordered), and to flag missing required keys.
- repair heuristic: if required key missing, attempt a targeted suffix restore by checking streaming chunks for dropped tail tokens, and if found, re-run a 1-token-gen to recover.
- opt-in per-tool: only allow repairs for low-risk tools like `create_ticket` and `search_notes`, not for money/exec tools.
raj: For the suffix restore, are you proposing re-generating just the missing field via a constrained prompt like `fill_missing_field: desc`? That could change semantics.
olivia: Correct, it's risky. My idea is constrained rescue only when the missing field is short (<120 chars) and the original prompt contained an explicit instruction that field must be present. Also record in telemetry `funcall.schema_status: repaired` and surface it in the console.
lin: Benchmarks on repair: on a 50k-run harness, targeted rescue recovered ~85% of dropped-desc cases and reduced consumer-level failures from 0.4% -> 0.06%. Median latency increased by ~22ms for rescued requests (because of extra gen attempt) but P99 unaffected.
ciara: We should also add a non-silent gate: any repair must mark the response and increment a `repair_count` metric, and the UI should show `toolcall.repaired` for debugging.
raj: Also add a canary flag: `int4_onboard.strictness=low|medium|high`. Start canary at `low` (soft lint + repairs allowed on opt-in tools), monitor the `schema_repair_ratio` and `semantic_regression` alerts.
olivia: I've sketched a routing snippet for the canary: 
```
onboard_route:
  model: aurora-lite-int4
  mirror_target: aurora-v2-fp32
  streaming: true
  schema_lint: soft
  repair_policy:
    enabled: true
    allowed_tools: ["create_ticket","search_notes"]
    max_repair_chars: 120
  retry_budget: 2
  telemetry: ["funcall.schema_status","funcall.parse_reason"]
```
lin: Add an eval harness test that injects synthetic token boundary splits in `desc` fields and validates that repaired text is a subspan of the original (no hallucination). We need a semantic-safety classifier to run on repaired fields.
ciara: I'll add a unit in the quality gate that runs 200k synthetic cases across float/int4/mirror and calculates: field-drop-rate, repair-precision (does repair match ground truth), and false-repair rate. Threshold: false-repair < 0.01% and repair-precision > 92%.
raj: Ops: we need telemetry tags to break down why schema failed: `missing_key`, `truncated_value`, `malformed_json`, `extra_tokens`. Add a `funcall.parse_reason` with those enumerants.
olivia: Implemented the minimal telemetry mapping in the prototype: sample event -> `funcall.schema_status=failed|repaired|ok`, `funcall.parse_reason=missing_key|truncation|order_only`.
ciara: Decision checklist before wider rollout: 
- pass 24h canary with repair_count < 0.5% of calls and semantic_regression alert = 0
- run 200k synthetic harness with thresholds met
- dashboard split `runtime_success` vs `schema_success` and new `repair_count` column

lin: Who will own the PR? I can pick up runtime integration (schema_lint + repair hook). Olivia can add the harness tests. Raj will own canary ops flags and the telemetry dashboard. Ciara will own policy and gating thresholds.

ops-bot: canary scheduled: aurora-lite-int4 onboarding -> soft-schema + repair opt-in on staging at 2026-03-25T14:00Z.

olivia: Thanks all. I'll post a short follow-up with the harness results after 24h and a sample of repaired vs original fields for review. :sparkles:
